jamie: quick sync — i'm about to open the PR to remove the legacy `binding_mapper` table and switch callers to `permission_shape`. plan attached below, need sec/infra eyes on kms/audit implications before canary.

maria: thanks. high level: how are we preserving audit lineage? any change to the KMS envelope or kid usage? :thinking_face: 

jamie: not changing KMS envelope. migration writes a `legacy_mapping` row that references old binding ids, then copies normalized claims into `permission_shape`. KMS keys are used only for signing audit events — no ciphertext changes. still want to confirm we don't inadvertently rotate kids mid-canary.

lee: can you paste the migration snippet? i'll run a quick dry on a snapshot.

jamie: sure — snippet: ```sql
-- idempotent backfill: normalize nulls and collapse duplicates
INSERT INTO permission_shape (principal_id, resource, role, source, migrated_at)
SELECT principal_id, resource, COALESCE(role, 'reader') AS role, 'binding_mapper_migration', now()
FROM binding_mapper
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM permission_shape p
  WHERE p.principal_id = binding_mapper.principal_id
    AND p.resource = binding_mapper.resource
    AND p.role = COALESCE(binding_mapper.role, 'reader')
);
```

kevin: note — our KMS key rotation job runs hourly between :00 and :10. if the canary overlaps that window we could see kid churn in audit entries. i'd recommend scheduling canary outside rotation or pin audit-kid via job label.

maria: also: any nullable roles in binding_mapper? late edgecases killed us before. we should log counts pre/post and add a small regression check.

jamie: yes there are ~0.15% null roles historically. plan includes preflight SQL that reports counts and sample principals. preflight: ```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN role IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_roles
FROM binding_mapper;
```

audit-bot: [audit] migration_preflight: shard=shard-7 total=243027 null_roles=354 (0.145%). snapshot_id=snap-2024-06-25T09:12:34Z

lee: quick heads-up from dry-run: when role is NULL and resource has a legacy override we saw a mapping that produced an empty role -> policy engine returns implicit deny for some service accounts.

sre-oncall: that implicit deny will show up as elevated 403 alerts in prod. we should add a soft-fallback policy for the canary window to map NULL->reader at the policy-eval layer until backfill completes. easier than rolling back DB.

jamie: i like that. action items: 1) kevin to schedule canary outside kms rotation or pin kid (owner: kevin, eta: today EOD). 2) lee to run full preflight and produce sample of affected principals (owner: lee, eta: 2h). 3) maria to sign off on audit retention/lineage checks (owner: maria, eta: 4h). 4) sre-oncall to deploy soft-fallback rule and monitor 403 spike (owner: sre-oncall, eta: 1h). i'll open the PR with feature-flag gating the destructive drop.

kevin: canary scheduled for 2024-06-26T14:00 UTC (outside rotation). will also set env var AUDIT_KID_PIN=ck-2024-06 until canary completes.

lee: preflight results posted to the runbook: sample principals include two service accounts owned by billing svc. i'll whitelist them in the fallback mapping. also attaching quick patch to migration that uses `COALESCE(role, 'reader')` to avoid null deny.

maria: please add an eval: pick 100 random recent requests from those principals and confirm identical enforcement before/after. if we see >=1% divergence we stop.

jamie: agreed. i'll also add observability: per-principal diff metric + tokenized sample stored in s3 for 7 days.

audit-bot: [audit] migration_canary_started: canary_id=canary-172980 fseeds=5 shards=[shard-7]

sre-oncall: monitoring: alert rule created `canary-403-surge` -> pager if >50 403s over 5m.

jamie: thanks all, i'll coordinate post-canary retrospective. closing thread when PR merges. :white_check_mark:
